subject: Performance spike in MedTechX private cluster — immediate mitigation & exec visibility
messages:
From: Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:31:12 +0200
Subject: Sudden p95 latency + 502s on private cluster since 05:00 CEST

Hi Markus / Mina,

We started seeing a large increase in p95 latency and ~1-2% 502 errors on our private on-prem inference cluster starting around 05:00 CEST. The behavior coincided with the maintenance window where our ops team applied the 1.4.2 kernel patch and a new batching config that your team recommended last week.

Quick facts:
- Affected: medtechx-prod: inference service (p95 from 180ms -> 1.2s; throughput down ~30%)
- Error pattern: transient 502s, correlated with long tail request spikes and KV cache misses
- We attached a log bundle (diagnostics-20280520.zip) and a screenshot of the latency graph.

This is customer-impacting. Can you confirm whether a rollback of the kernel patch is possible from your side, or if you have an immediate mitigation? We need an ETA — our product leadership is already on the call.

Thanks,
Danielle Choi
SRE Lead, MedTechX
attachments: diagnostics-20280520.zip, metrics-snap-20280520.png
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:38:45 +0200
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency + 502s on private cluster since 05:00 CEST

Danielle — thanks for the heads up and the bundle. I’ve pulled in Mina (on-call infra lead), Laura (CS lead), and Vivek (Private deployments).

Short answers up front:
1) We see the same signal in our tracing and the call logs you sent.
2) We suspect the kernel patch + new batching policy interacted with KV cache eviction behavior, creating cold-cache amplification under your workload mix.

Plan: Mina will triage and tell us if a rollback is required. Vivek, can you confirm whether we can execute an emergency rollback / temporary config change without breaking the control plane? If not, we need a stop-gap (drop batching depth to 1, force prefix cache hotness).

I’m marking this P0. I’ll escalate to the executive on-call if we need reserved capacity or priority remote hours. 

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:02:18 +0200
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency + 502s on private cluster since 05:00 CEST

On Mon, May 20, 2028 at 08:31, Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a large increase in p95 latency...

I pulled the logs. Preliminary findings:
- KV cache miss rate spiked ~18% after the new batching config (max_batch_tokens=4096) was applied. We’re seeing longer decode tails due to increased tensor allocation churn and an unexpected kernel scheduler latency bump for small, high-QPS requests.
- The kernel patch changed how page reclaim interacts with pinned GPU pages on this distro (RHEL-8.8 variant). That causes occasional stalls when the runtime attempts to preempt large memcpy ops.

Immediate mitigations we can attempt remotely (low risk, quick):
- Reduce max_batch_tokens to 512 and lower max_concurrency on the hotspot model route (reduces tail amplification).
- Flip on aggressive prefix hotness promotion (increase kv_cache_prefill_ratio).

If the mitigations do not restore p95 within 20–30 minutes, I recommend a controlled rollback of the kernel patch. That requires a short maintenance window with on-prem ops, which Vivek can coordinate.

I’ll start with the config flip now and post updates.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:15:34 +0200
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency + 502s on private cluster since 05:00 CEST

Markus / team — quick operational note:
- We do have the ability to orchestrate a kernel rollback but it requires a short gate with MedTechX ops (we need their on-site orchestration step). If Mina’s config changes are effective, we can avoid the rollback.
- If we proceed with rollback, target impact window: ~12 minutes node-by-node (coordination + quick smoke tests). We’ll run rollback on 2 nodes first (canary) and watch the hotpath.

Requesting exec visibility because MedTechX leadership is asking for priority SLA remediation and possible bill credit/contract concession if this is from our recommended config changes. Markus — do you want me to prepare a short exec note with options (1: config flip, 2: rollback + emergency hours, 3: reserved GPU burst) to route to GTM?

— Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:40:50 +0200
Subject: Executive brief: MedTechX private cluster incident (P0)

Team — short summary for leadership / finance:
- Impact: MedTechX production inference p95 increased from 180ms -> 1.2s; 1–2% 502s; throughput -30% since 05:00 CEST during their maintenance window.
- Likely root cause: interaction between 1.4.2 kernel patch and our new batching profile causing KV cache miss amplification and occasional GPU memcpy preemption stalls.
- Options and ask:
  1) Attempt config mitigation (low risk, ~5–10min to apply). Recommended first step.
  2) If remediation fails, authorize an emergency kernel rollback with MedTechX ops (expected node-level disruption for ~12min per node). Need approval for priority engineering hours and possible travel/onsite support.
  3) As contingency, offer reserved burst capacity for 24 hours (paid at standard emergency rate) to route critical traffic away from the private cluster while we remediate.

Please approve option 1 immediately. If option 1 fails in 30 minutes, I request go-ahead for option 2 and assignment of 2 senior infra engineers for the rollback window. Laura — please prepare proposed credit language if we proceed to option 2.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:05:10 +0200
Subject: Re: Executive brief: MedTechX private cluster incident (P0)

Approved: option 1 now. If no improvement in 30 minutes, approve option 2 (rollback) — assign Mina + Vivek as the on-call rollback pair. I’ll notify customer success and finance to draft credit language (preliminary 10% monthly credit placeholder until postmortem).

Action items I’ll own:
- Notify account exec and schedule a 15-min join in 20 minutes for a live smoke check.
- Draft credit language and hold for final decision after root cause confirmation.
- Share runbook link for rollback steps: DOCS-RTB-4721.

— Laura
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Choi <danielle.choi@medtechx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 16:45:00 +0200
Subject: MedTechX status update & planned rollback window (if needed)

Danielle — thanks for patience while we triaged. Quick status:
- Mina’s config mitigation (max_batch_tokens=512, kv_cache_prefill_ratio increased) reduced p95 from ~1.2s -> ~260ms within 12 minutes and error rate dropped under 0.2%.
- We kept the change under observation for 24 hours. Metrics are stable but we recommend a conservative kernel rollback on one affected node to confirm the hypothesis and eliminate the remaining tail microglitch.

Proposed rollback window (can be cancelled if you prefer):
- Wednesday 22 May 2028, 09:00–09:30 CEST (on-site orchestrated rollback; canary two nodes, then pause for 20 min).
- Redwood will provide 2 senior infra engineers and a runbook. Expected single-node downtime ~12 minutes during the step, no customer request reroute required.

If you’re comfortable, please confirm the window and we’ll send the final runbook + pre-check list. If you prefer to skip rollback (metrics stable), we’ll schedule a low-risk maintenance exercise next week instead.

Thanks — and again, apologies for the disruption. We’ll follow up with a postmortem and proposed credit if the rollback is needed.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
